mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a quarter indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and consumer confidence improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over a quarter indicates a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it signals a slowdown in economic output and potential recessionary pressures.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 2% within a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) suggests accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors seek higher returns in equities.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both UNRATE increased and PAYEMS decreased within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising retail sales (RSAFS) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) over a quarter signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity and consumer confidence improve.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases and UNRATE decreases in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased and UNRATE decreased within a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4%) during a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) suggests a misaligned monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the real economy struggles under high borrowing costs.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and CPIAUCSL was below 2%.
